article.title: vlt 1.0 Ships as an npm-Compatible Package Registry With Phased Installs and Malware-Blocking
article.summary: vlt, built by npm's original developers, launched a 1.0 client and hosted registry that splits install from script execution and blocks flagged malware before delivery.
article.body_markdown:
## Overview

vlt, a JavaScript package manager and registry built by the original creators of npm, has released vlt 1.0, shipping as a drop-in npm replacement alongside the general availability of its hosted package registries and ecosystem mirrors, according to [InfoQ](https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/09/vlt-npm-replacement/). The company's own announcement, published by founder and CEO Darcy Clarke on the [vlt blog](https://www.vlt.io/blog/1-0), says the release makes vlt "now an end-to-end platform for developers, their teams and agents to ship faster, safer, and more reliably."

## What We Know

- vlt 1.0 introduces phased installations that stop dependency scripts from running automatically, a queryable dependency graph with more than 60 CSS-like selectors, and hosted registries that reject known-malicious packages before they are served, as reported by [InfoQ](https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/09/vlt-npm-replacement/).
- Where npm downloads, extracts, and runs lifecycle scripts in a single step, vlt splits the process in two: `vlt install` downloads and extracts packages without executing anything, while `vlt build` then runs scripts only for trusted packages, according to [InfoQ](https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/09/vlt-npm-replacement/). vlt's own blog describes the same mechanism, saying phased installations allow `vlt install` "to download without running scripts" and `vlt build` "to run selectively, blocking known malware by default," per the [vlt announcement](https://www.vlt.io/blog/1-0).
- The `vlt query` command treats the dependency graph like a DOM tree using a dependency selector syntax. Around half of the more than 60 selectors are security-focused and powered by a Socket integration, and a `:host(local)` selector extends queries across every project on a machine, while a `--view=mermaid` flag renders matched dependencies as a diagram, according to [InfoQ](https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/09/vlt-npm-replacement/). vlt's own blog lists examples of the selectors, including `:malware`, `:cve`, `:unmaintained`, `:outdated`, `:eval`, `:fs`, `:license`, `:vuln`, `:peer`, and `:dist()`, per the [vlt announcement](https://www.vlt.io/blog/1-0).
- Founder Darcy Clarke announced the release on X, describing a client "built so nothing runs on your machine just because you typed install," as reported by [InfoQ](https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/09/vlt-npm-replacement/).
- vlt says it has flagged more than 275,000 package versions as malicious, with a quarter of them still installable on the public npm registry, according to [InfoQ](https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/09/vlt-npm-replacement/); vlt's own announcement puts the same figures at "over 275k package versions" flagged, with "over 25% of them still being actively available for download" on npm, per the [vlt blog](https://www.vlt.io/blog/1-0).
- vlt reports its hosted registry as up to 38% faster than npm, though pnpm and Bun still lead on raw install speed overall, according to [InfoQ](https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/09/vlt-npm-replacement/). vlt's own site shows the same 38% figure alongside benchmark numbers of 12.0 seconds versus npm's 19.4 seconds for an Astro project installation, per [vlt's homepage](https://www.vlt.io/).
- The launch reached the front page of Hacker News, where one commenter wrote "This will benefit the entire ecosystem," while another asked plainly, "I am not sure exactly what this service is or why it is desirable. Pitch me in five seconds or less?" according to the [Hacker News discussion](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49172251). Clarke replied in the thread: "5s: save time & money," followed by a longer pitch about reducing supply-chain risk and lowering infrastructure costs.
- Migrating an existing project requires running `npm install -g vlt`, then `vlt install` and `vlt build`, with configuration moving from `.npmrc` to `vlt.json` and a new `vlt-lock.json` lockfile; the npm-compatible registry API keeps existing CI pipelines and tooling working, according to [InfoQ](https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/09/vlt-npm-replacement/). vlt is free and open source under a BSD-2-Clause-Patent license, developed by vlt technology inc., per [InfoQ](https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/09/vlt-npm-replacement/).

## Context

The release follows a year of high-profile npm supply-chain attacks, including the Shai-Hulud worm, and comes after other tools already tightened their own defaults: npm v12 now disables install scripts by default, as [previously reported](/article/2026-07/13-npm-v12-ships-with-install-scripts-disabled-by-default-after-a-year-of-supply-chain-attacks) by The Machine Herald, while pnpm quarantines fresh releases with a minimum release age, a change The Machine Herald also [previously covered](/article/2026-04/22-pnpm-11-rc-makes-a-24-hour-release-delay-the-default-turning-a-supply-chain-workaround-into-a-baseline). Bun blocks postinstall scripts as well, according to [InfoQ](https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/09/vlt-npm-replacement/). vlt's registries go further than any of those defaults by rejecting malicious packages at the registry level rather than only restricting what runs on a developer's machine, per [InfoQ](https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/09/vlt-npm-replacement/).

## What We Don't Know

- InfoQ's coverage does not specify exactly how vlt's malware-detection pipeline decides which of the 275,000-plus flagged package versions to block versus merely flag, beyond the general description of rejecting "known-malicious packages" at the registry.
- Adoption figures — how many teams or CI pipelines have migrated to vlt's client or hosted registries since the August 4 announcement — were not disclosed in any of the sources reviewed.
